Destruction Warlock Rotation in The War Within

Destruction excels at dealing large hits through Chaos Bolt and very strong cleave damage through Havoc . Destruction is by nature a relatively simple spec to play, but with a different Soul Shards system than Affliction and Demonology, the playstyle is quite different.
When playing Destruction, your rotation includes:

 
 

 
 Soul Shard management Do not overcap Soul Shards. Destruction's Soul Shards resource is different than Affliction and Demonology, as all our shards are split into 10 soul shard fragments. We have great control over generating and spending this resource, so make sure you're aware of having Soul Shards when you need them, while not wasting any Soul Shards by overcapping. 
 

 

 
 

 
 Cooldown management: Being able to properly manage your cooldowns, such as Havoc and Summon Infernal will make a big difference in how much damage you're doing. Making sure you have the correct amount of Soul Shards before using these, and making sure you don't lose out on any uses, is a big difference maker between high DPS and low DPS. 
 

 

 
 
 
 Movement: When you're moving around, you only have very few ways to deal damage. You can play around with always casting abilities such as Conflagrate while running, but odds are you're going to lose out on DPS. That means, playing movement segments correctly will be a big difference maker. Utilizing abilities like Demonic Circle and Demonic Gateway properly will help you with that. 
 

 

If you're looking for a more bite-sized rotation explanation, check out our simplified guide below:

Pre-Combat Check

 Before any combat happens, it is important for Destruction Warlock to make sure the following are done. This applies to raids, dungeons, delves, or even open-world content.

 Single Button Rotation Assistant Losses for Destruction Warlock 

Destruction has a relatively simple rotation that works by generating Soul Shards and spending that resource on damage-dealing spells. Compared to other DPS specs, we have a lower number of main abilities in our rotation. For this reason, the rotational tool might not actually be that horrible percentagewise compared to a lot of other specs. That being said, using the rotational tool is not going to be the way you get the most out of your character, but for a casual player just running through non challenging content you will be able to get away with using it.

Rotation Assist Losses for Destruction Warlock

When using the Rotation Assist, you can expect the following losses when compared to performing your rotation yourself:

 Single Target 
 
Assisted Highlight: About ~3.8% DPS Loss 

Single-Button Assistant: About ~10.4% DPS Loss 
 

 Note - These numbers assume the player manually casts Summon Infernal , which is not being highlighted by neither the rotation assist or the single-button helper. If you do not manually remember to use Summon Infernal , your DPS loss is going to be significantly higher.

 AoE 
 
Assisted Highlight: About ~11% DPS Loss 

Single-Button Assistant: About ~14% DPS Loss 
 

 Note - For AoE it's a little hard deciding what to expect. It's going to vary heavily on wether or not you manually pop your Summon Infernal and Havoc , because the helper does not do this. The numbers above assume neither of these are manually popped on AoE, so if you do manually pop them regardless you can expect a lower DPS loss.

Destruction Warlock Cooldowns Not Used by Rotation Assist

When using both the assisted highlighting and the single-button assistant, you will need to use the following cooldowns manually, because they will not automatically be used by the one-button assistant. Both of these cooldowns are important for the Destruction DPS output, and if they're not used at all the expected DPS loss is going to be significantly worse than the numbers presented above. For more information on how to properly use these cooldowns, there is a segment further down in this guide explaining more in depth.

Click to expand list of cooldowns

 
 Summon Infernal

A way to combat this slightly is opting to pick up Mayhem rather than Havoc . While Havoc might be a better option a lot of the time, Mayhem is much better than having Havoc and not using it.

 Destruction Warlock Major Cooldown Usage

Destruction has a number of both big and small cooldowns that are important to know how to play in order to succeed.

 Summon Infernal is our 2-minute cooldown that helps us generate more Soul Shards during its duration. Some things to keep in mind when using your infernal is:
 
If you're playing Crashing Chaos , your Infernal cast also makes your damage more important. It's not only a point and click cooldown that does damage on its own; make sure you pair this up with any racial ability and trinkets if you can.

Keep in mind you can delay this cooldown as long as you don't miss out on uses. During a Mythic+ dungeon you will likely want to pop this as often as possible because you will lose out on uses otherwise, but popping it at the correct time is important.
 

I have already covered Havoc very thoroughly in this guide, but I will just recap the important points here:
 
Keep in mind you can generate 2x Soul Shards with Havoc while your spenders don't cost extra.

 Havoc only replicates 60% of the damage of your single-target abilities, meaning you should apply this to the less important target.

Make sure your target is going to live for the full Havoc duration if possible.
 

When playing Destruction, you can gain a good portion of damage by knowing what each of the demons summoned by the hero talent tree does:

Because of the talent Touch of Rancora , and because of how Destruction works, you want to trigger your demons by casting a Chaos Bolt . This is unless you're in a situation where you're damaging a LOT of targets, and in that situation you should probably be playing .
 
 Demonic Art: Overlord - Charges your target and does a frontal cleave. Enemies hit by this cleave then takes increased damage from you and your demons because of the talent Cloven Souls . If the target you cast on to trigger the Demonic Art: Overlord dies before the overlord reaches the target, it instead swaps to a different target and hits that one. Keep this in mind, because if you're damaging a lot of targets, try not to trigger this onto a target that is standing alone. Try to aim this into a big pack for the most damage. Also, keep in mind your damage is increased to targets hit by this for 15 seconds, so try to hit those targets.

 Demonic Art: Mother of Chaos - Summons next to you and starts channelling damage into your target. Additionally, triggering this demonic art changes your next Incinerate into Infernal Bolt which deals increased damage and generates 2 full Soul Shards. Make sure you do not overcap on Soul Shards by casting this. Instead, cast Chaos Bolt to go down to at least 2,5 Soul Shards, but ideally below 2 Soul Shards before casting Infernal Bolt . Also, the abilitiy Demonic Art: Mother of Chaos casts when summoned is a channelled AoE, which might not always start rechannelling onto a new target if the target dies during this channel. For that reason, try to cast this onto a target that's going to live for the full duration.

 Demonic Art: Pit Lord - Is also summoned right next to you, and starts dealing pulsating AoE damage onto and around your target. Additionally, triggering this Demonic Art turns your next Chaos Bolt into Ruination . A very powerful AoE around your target. Make sure you cast this on the mob where it's going to hit the most targets possible.
 

Some extra notes when palying Diabolist is, that you always cycle in the same order. It goes:
 
Overlord

Mother of Chaos

Pit Lord
 
This resets on boss combat in raids, but not in dungeons. This means, you can play slower or faster from time to time, depending on what demon you want to summon. As an example, if you're in a dungeon and you're about to finish off a pack, just killing off the last few mobs, and you're about to gain Demonic Art: Pit Lord , do not trigger this on that pack. Instead, be a little patient and deal big damage on the next pack. Do not postpone this, because when playing, you do cycle through the rotation of demons fairly quickly. However, it adds a layer of complexity and depth to the playstyle and might ultimately make your damage output significantly higher.

Before pressing Malevolence , always have all of your Wither applied. This can happen by you doing a big pull, casting Cataclysm -> Channel Demonfire and then following it up by Malevolence into either Chaos Bolt or Rain of Fire spam, collapsing your Wither stacks, dealing damage with Blackened Soul . 

During Malevolence , all of the Soul Shards you cast grants double stacks of Wither to your targets, so try your very best to have some shards ready before, and make sure you dump as much as you can before Malevolence runs out. And be careful not to let your Wither drop on high stacks.

On 1-3 targets, spend Soul Shards on Chaos Bolt . On 4+ use Rain of Fire . When moving and about to cap on Soul Shards, cast Shadowburn .
This is when you're about to proc your Diabolist demon. You want to use a Chaos Bolt to do so to benefit from the increased damage, as well as the reduced cast time.
Make sure you read the section below on what soul shard spender you should use in what situation. This is for single-target, so Chaos Bolt is the best bet, but in general, make sure you're aware of what soul-shard spender you should use in what situation.

Comment by suchtie 
Since the guide still doesn't mention it at all, even as the patch is almost over, here's the 11.0 Hellcaller deal for those who haven't gone elsewhere to look it up.

Assuming the Hellcaller M+ build from the Talents page.

Opener:
 
Cast Cataclysm so that it finishes as the boss/trash pack is pulled/in position

 Conflagrate 

 Shadowburn 

 Channel Demonfire 

 Summon Infernal 

Use any trinkets and racials

 Malevolence 

Continue regular rotation
 

The goal of the opener is to get Wither applied to as many targets as possible, use Channel Demonfire to increase the DoT's duration to the max, and only then get your CDs going so that you can focus on generating and spending as many soul shards as possible while your Infernal and Malevolence are up. Conflagrate and Shadowburn are used early to get charges rolling, and it's best to have Roaring Blaze for Channel Demonfire .

If you're pulling a boss with a timer, you can precast Incinerate at 3 seconds to pull.

For the rest of the rotation, use the guide's respective sections. Immolate becomes Wither , of course.

As for Malevolence , just use it on cooldown. Make sure that as many targets as possible have Wither beforehand. You can delay Malevolence slightly if you know that adds which will live longer than 10-ish seconds will spawn/be pulled soon, and Cataclysm will be ready for it. If it's just a few mobs, you can also manually apply Wither to each. But don't delay Malevolence too long because you want to align it with your Infernal.

 Malevolence should be cast after Summon Infernal since its duration is shorter.

While Malevolence and/or Infernal are up, spend soul shards aggressively. Try to use as many spenders as possible to get the most out of your CDs.

In singletarget situations, you should pool a few soul shards (3-4) in preparation for your CDs. Don't pool shards in AoE because all of your Withers and Rain of Fire will generate tons of shards, and you don't want to overcap.

Cast Channel Demonfire while Roaring Blaze is up. This is less important for AoE.

If anyone has further tips or corrections, please comment!
